h1: Relax Inn Rayong (Ban Phe) — a small guesthouse across from the pier with the easiest access to Koh Samet
intro: Picture this: you wake up, walk a few steps across the road, and you're at the pier ready to hop on the ferry to Koh Samet — no rushing to check out before sunrise. Relax Inn is a small 2-star guesthouse in the Ban Phe area of Phe sub-district, Mueang Rayong district, sitting right across from the Ban Phe pier, which makes it a popular base for anyone heading to Koh Samet or just back from the island · There are only 10 rooms, simply furnished but clean, some with sea-view balconies, plus an on-site bar and restaurant with a pool table and free parking · From about THB 600/night · It scores 8.2, a "very good" rating, from over 362 reviews, and the things people mention most are the location by the pier and how friendly the owner is.

body.html: Who Relax Inn is right for — to put it as simply as possible, Relax Inn is a small guesthouse for people who treat Ban Phe as a "stopover" on the way to Koh Samet rather than a destination where they want luxury · It isn't a beachfront resort with a pool, and it isn't a big chain hotel with full facilities, but a place of just 10 rooms in the Ban Phe area of Phe sub-district, Mueang Rayong district, across from the pier where the ferries cross to Koh Samet · Real reviews line up on this: the people it suits are budget travelers, couples on a short trip, and international backpackers who want a single night before or after taking the ferry to the island · The draw here isn't luxury but a location that's a few steps from the pier, rooms that are cleaner than the price suggests, and an owner so friendly that many people remember them · Another group who say it's worth it are those who drive in themselves and want somewhere safe to leave the car while they're out on the island, because there's free parking here · In short, it's a place that plays on the words "convenient and good value" for a Koh Samet trip, in exchange for no pool and no big-hotel level of service — something most guests understand and accept before they even book.

Location and getting around — this is Relax Inn's number-one selling point, no question · The guesthouse sits in the Ban Phe area of Phe sub-district, Mueang Rayong district, across from the pier where the ferries to Koh Samet depart · According to the property, Nuan Thip pier and the speedboat departure point for Koh Samet are only about 170 meters away, while Nuan Thip Market is just about 90 meters off, an easy walk for food and supplies · This is why a lot of people choose to stay here — instead of waking before dawn to drive from the city center or Pattaya to catch the first ferry, you just walk a few steps across the road to the pier · The ferry across to Koh Samet takes about 30 min, or less by speedboat · For mainland sights, Mae Ramphueng Beach and Suan Son Beach are about 1.6 km away, Ban Phe Market is close by, and Khao Laem Ya–Mu Ko Samet National Park is about 6 km · Rayong Botanical Garden and the Rayong Aquarium are also a short drive away · One thing to note about longer journeys: U-Tapao Airport (UTP) is about 60–67 km away, roughly an hour plus, and there's no airport shuttle, so you'll need to arrange a ride or drive yourself · The other thing to be straight about is that the Ban Phe pier area is busy with plenty of traffic during the day, so some reviews mention road noise and an atmosphere that isn't the quiet calm of a resort tucked away in the forest.

"Just a few steps across the road and you're at the pier for the ferry to Koh Samet — no need to rush over before dawn · The room is small but very clean, and the owner is kind and gave us all the tips on ferries and restaurants — great value for a single night before heading to the island."

Room types and decor — Relax Inn is a small property with only about 10 rooms in all, which gives it a homey, friendly feel rather than a hotel one · The main rooms come in just a few types, starting with the Superior Double, which has one king bed and, in some rooms, a sea view, moving up to the Superior Twin with two single beds for friends or travelers who want separate beds, and the Comfort Triple, which sleeps three for a small group or family · The decor is the simple guesthouse style — not focused on luxe design but on being clean and genuinely usable · Every room has air conditioning, a wardrobe, a private bathroom with a shower and water heater, free toiletries, and free Wi-Fi · The thing real reviews praise most consistently is the cleanliness of the rooms; many say the rooms are small but spotless, with good water-heater pressure and air conditioning that cools quickly · Some rooms have a private balcony looking out to a sea view or the pier neighborhood, a detail worth requesting at the time of booking if it matters to you, because not every room gets a sea view · To be straight about it, as a budget guesthouse the rooms are compact, better suited to a short overnight than lounging all day, and they don't have the full in-room amenities of a big hotel — for example, not every room has a minibar or safe, which is normal for this type of place and is reflected in what you pay.

Facilities — you should understand first that Relax Inn is a small guesthouse, so there's no swimming pool and none of the luxe facilities of a resort · But what it does have covers a traveler's needs well · The highlight many reviews mention is the on-site bar and restaurant with a relaxed feel and a pool table to play, a corner to sip a cold beer and chat with other travelers or the owner in the evening · Beyond that there's an outdoor terrace, a shared lounge, a small cafe and snack bar, luggage storage, a laundry service (extra charge), and a small fitness room (extra charge) · The thing that's really handy for a Koh Samet trip is the free parking and luggage storage, so people who drive in can park and leave their bags with peace of mind before taking the ferry across · There's free Wi-Fi in the common areas and in the rooms · To be straight, these facilities are the "basics, all there for a short stay" kind — not luxe, but for value at a property by the pier at this price they're a fair amount to get · Anyone expecting a pool, a full gym, or a spa should look at a beachfront resort in the Mae Ramphueng area or on Koh Samet instead.

Food and the bar — what sets Relax Inn apart from your average guesthouse is the on-site bar and restaurant, which gets praise for its atmosphere · A number of international reviews mention the restaurant and bar attached to the property as having a nice atmosphere, good food, cold beer, and a pool table to play in the evening · It's a corner where guests traveling solo or as a couple can sit back, chat, and get to know other travelers in a relaxed guesthouse setting · To be straight, this property doesn't include breakfast in the room rate, but that's barely an issue because the location helps a lot — Nuan Thip Market is only about 90 meters away, a few steps to find breakfast, local bites, and fresh seafood, and the Ban Phe area is also full of seafood spots, coffee shops, and reasonably priced made-to-order restaurants · So many people choose to head out for food rather than eat at the property every meal, which is part of the charm of staying in the middle of a pier neighborhood with food all around · Overall, food at Relax Inn isn't the reason to come and eat on site, but the in-house bar and restaurant are an extra that makes the stay feel much warmer and more welcoming.

Service — service is another area that gets steady praise in real reviews, and may be this place's strongest point aside from the location · As a small property run by the owner, the owner and staff are often described as friendly, kind, and very helpful · What many reviews are especially impressed by is that the owner speaks several languages — Thai, English, and French (with Chinese and Italian listed as well) — which makes international travelers comfortable asking about ferries, schedules, restaurants, and places to visit · Quite a few reviews tell of the owner helping with how to get to Koh Samet, sorting out ferry tickets, and giving honest travel advice · The family-style front desk makes people who arrive and leave at flexible times feel at ease · But to be straight, as a small place run family-style, some service standards aren't as polished or systematic as a big chain hotel — for example, the set check-in window of 2:00 PM–8:00 PM may not be flexible for those arriving very late, and at times when the owner is away it can take longer to coordinate · Overall, the owner's warmth and friendliness are what leave many guests impressed and saying they'd come back.

What real reviews say (the good and the not-so-good) — pulled together from Trip.com, Booking.com, Agoda, and TripAdvisor, the picture is fairly consistent · On the praise side: the location across from the pier, a few steps to the ferry departure point for Koh Samet; rooms that are small but spotless, with good water-heater pressure and new, fast-cooling air conditioning; a friendly owner who speaks several languages and is very helpful; an on-site bar and restaurant with a nice atmosphere and a pool table; free parking and luggage storage, handy for people heading to the island; and prices that are great value among the places by the pier · On the watch-out side: the thing mentioned most is the noise and bustle of the pier area — Ban Phe has plenty of traffic and people during the day, so rooms facing the road or on lower floors may catch some outside noise · Next is the compact room size typical of a budget guesthouse, the lack of a pool and breakfast, and the small count of just 10 rooms, which fills up fast on long weekends · There's also a note about the set check-in window of 2:00 PM–8:00 PM, which late arrivals should flag in advance · Most of these gripes can be eased by setting expectations to match the type of place and choosing a quieter room toward the back, rather than being problems that keep most people from returning.

"The room was very clean and the owner was lovely, giving us all the tips on the ferry to Koh Samet · My only gripe is that the pier area is crowded during the day with some road noise — next time I'll ask for a quieter room toward the back. Everything else is great value for a spot right across from the pier like this."

Price and value — the starting price for the smallest room, the Superior Double, is about THB 600/night on weekdays in low season, climbing to around THB 800–1,200+ on weekends, long weekends, or in high season when everyone flocks to Koh Samet · Rooms that sleep more, like the Comfort Triple, go higher with the number of people · Compared with places in the Ban Phe area and Rayong city center, Relax Inn feels like great value among budget stays right by the pier · What makes it worth it is a location that saves both time and travel costs — instead of paying for a pricey stay in the city or Pattaya and then waking before dawn to drive over for the ferry, you just sleep here for a night and walk across the road to the boat · Add free parking, luggage storage, and an owner who helps sort out the ferry, and every baht you spend on this location pays off in full for a Koh Samet trip · But if you're expecting a pool, a large room, breakfast, or a quiet beachfront atmosphere, this price honestly reflects what it is — a small guesthouse by the pier, not a resort — and you should look at a different type of place instead.

Good to know before booking — a few things help the stay go more smoothly · One, since there are only 10 rooms, the place fills up fast on long weekends and in high season when lots of people head to Koh Samet, so book ahead and compare prices across platforms · Two, check-in is set for 2:00 PM–8:00 PM and check-out is before 12:00 PM, so if you arrive late or your ferry back from the island lands very late, give the owner clear advance notice · Three, if you're a light sleeper or sensitive to noise, ask for a room toward the back that doesn't face the road, since the pier area is busy during the day · Four, if you want a balcony or sea view, request it at booking time because not every room has a view · Five, the property has no breakfast, but markets and restaurants are an easy walk away — plan breakfast at Nuan Thip Market or one of the spots near the pier · Six, if you drive in, the upside is free parking and luggage storage, ideal for leaving the car while you're out on the island, but ask about available spaces during busy periods · Seven, go with free cancellation while your plans are still uncertain, because ferry schedules and the weather can change things.

The bottom line — from all the real reviews, Relax Inn is the best fit for travelers who want an overnight stay in the Ban Phe area before or after Koh Samet, on a budget and in a location a few steps from the pier · The spot across from the pier, rooms cleaner than the price suggests, an on-site bar and restaurant with a nice atmosphere, a friendly owner who speaks several languages, plus free parking and luggage storage, make it good value enough that it's hard to find a rival at the same location and price · If you're after a beachfront resort with a pool, large rooms, breakfast, or a quiet atmosphere, this may not be the answer, and you should consider a resort in the Mae Ramphueng Beach area or a stay on Koh Samet instead · But for a Koh Samet trip where you want a convenient base by the pier, want to save money, and want a taste of family guesthouse friendliness — Relax Inn answers that need squarely, and it's why it has kept a "very good" rating among places in the Ban Phe area all along.

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — Relax Inn Rayong (Ban Phe)

faq.q: Where is Relax Inn · is it convenient for Koh Samet?
faq.a: The guesthouse is in the Ban Phe area of Phe sub-district, Mueang Rayong district, across from the pier where the ferries to Koh Samet depart · The pier and speedboat point are only about 170 meters away, a few steps across the road · Nuan Thip Market is close by at about 90 meters, and Mae Ramphueng and Suan Son beaches are about 1.6 km · A great fit for a single night before or after heading to Koh Samet.

faq.q: What's the starting price at Relax Inn · what room types are there?
faq.a: Prices start at about THB 600/night for the Superior Double on weekdays in low season · They climb to around THB 800–1,200+ on weekends and in high season · There's the Superior Double (King bed), Superior Twin (2 single beds), and Comfort Triple for 3 people · Some rooms have a sea-view balcony, so request it at booking time · Always compare across platforms before booking.

faq.q: Who is Relax Inn right for?
faq.a: A great fit for budget travelers, couples, and backpackers who want an overnight stay in Ban Phe before or after Koh Samet, a few steps from the pier, with free parking · If you're after a beachfront resort with a pool or breakfast, look at places in the Mae Ramphueng Beach area or on Koh Samet instead.

faq.q: Does Relax Inn have a pool and breakfast?
faq.a: This is a small guesthouse, so there's no swimming pool and no breakfast included in the room rate · But there's an on-site bar and restaurant with a pool table and a nice atmosphere · Breakfast isn't an issue because Nuan Thip Market and seafood restaurants are within walking distance · There's free Wi-Fi, free parking, and luggage storage.

faq.q: What's the noise and atmosphere like at Relax Inn?
faq.a: Many reviews agree the Ban Phe pier area is busy with plenty of traffic during the day, and rooms facing the road or on lower floors may catch some outside noise · If you're a light sleeper, it's best to ask for a quieter room toward the back at booking time · Overall the atmosphere is friendly, family guesthouse style, not the quiet calm of a beachfront resort.

faq.q: What time is check-in and check-out at Relax Inn · can I arrive late?
faq.a: Check-in is set for 2:00 PM–8:00 PM and check-out is before 12:00 PM · If you arrive later than that or your ferry back from the island lands very late, you should give the owner clear advance notice since it's a small place run by the owner · There's free parking and luggage storage, ideal for leaving the car and your bags while you're out on Koh Samet.
